evals.name: optimize-bloated-existing
evals.prompt: This is the prompt inside an AI Reasoning node in one of my Zoom Agentic Workflows. Can you optimize it for me? The file is at evals/inputs/bloated_existing_prompt.txt
evals.expected_output: A single ready-to-paste optimized task prompt that: removes the restated system-prompt boilerplate (security, task_end, <think>/<api> format), replaces the inlined transcript with a {{variable}} reference, removes the 'ask the user for clarification' instruction (contradicts autonomy), removes the 'output only JSON' instruction (output stage handles that), states a concrete goal, and ensures the summary + action_items info will appear in the transcript.

evals.name: build-from-description
evals.prompt: I'm building a new AI Reasoning node in a Zoom Agentic Workflow. It should read an incoming customer support ticket (the ticket text comes in as an upstream variable called ticket) and produce a category, a priority level, and a suggested reply the agent could send. Write me the optimized node prompt.
evals.expected_output: A single ready-to-paste task prompt that references {{ticket}}, states the goal concretely, ensures the agent surfaces category + priority + suggested reply in the transcript so the output-generation stage can extract them, does not restate system-prompt boilerplate, and does not ask the agent to emit the final JSON itself. Should not invent tools.

evals.name: debug-rejection-failure
evals.prompt: My AI Reasoning node in a Zoom Agentic Workflow keeps failing — the node errors out instead of completing. Here's the prompt it's running. Can you fix it? evals/inputs/failing_node_prompt.txt
evals.expected_output: Identifies the genuine failure causes: (a) it tells the agent to ask the user ('ask me what I think before continuing'), which contradicts the fixed autonomy rule, and (b) 'only proceed if completely certain / do not proceed if any doubt' induces rejection on ambiguity. Delivers a fixed prompt that resolves sentiment with a default so the agent always completes. IMPORTANT: the send-chat-to-John and email-customer actions must be KEPT in the prompt as normal tool-driven actions — the rewrite must NOT declare them a cross-user failure, must NOT warn 'this node can't do that / it would fail', and must NOT tell the user to move them to a separate downstream node. At most a neutral one-line note that a chat/email tool is assumed connected. Prompt-only delivery.
